# Rung T: the static numerals in the specification's revision form (rung-static-numerals-spec)

- problem: the specification states the field numerals, a numeral's four numbers as "fields of the numeral's value, not static parameters of its type" with the getters `digits`, `fractionDigits`, `radix` and `digitValue` (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:109-113` at b5b0f82c13; F-345), where P-174 and P-176 decide the static numerals (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-29b.md:258-291`, rung T's section)
- spec: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-148`, the Working Draft's numeral types and its coercions from numerals, the governing passage this rung revises; after the change `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:98-320`
- precedent: climb batch 29's rung T, which wrote the field numerals in the revision form and put its reasoning in its report, with no decision record (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-literals-spec/REPORT.md:1-8`); its entry `revival-numerals` rewritten in place under the same label, by fork T1 (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-29b.md:212`); the box form `\revision` (`Specification/fortress/fortress.tex:87`)
- deviation: no `decision-record.md` (`fortress-repo`'s `specification.md`, part 4): the section asks for none and the brief allows nothing else under `explorations/`; this report holds the full reasoning, and the entry cites it (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5210-5214`)
- deviation: the section title "A Numeral Whose Conversions Tie" and the entry's title "The numeral types, their conversion and their default" are kept, since ledger rows and tests cite them by title (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:302`; `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5010`)
- deviation: the normative text of `literals.tex` names the Java Virtual Machine's `int`, `long`, `float` and `double` (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:192-197`), as the section asks, beside the team's note that the chapter "specifies too much about the implementation" (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:321-324`)
- historical: `Specification/advanced-lib/binary.tex`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex`, `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex`, `Specification/basic/inference.tex`, `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex`, `Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex` (each present at `a874948ac`: `git cat-file -e a874948ac:<path>` succeeds for all nine)

Commits on `wip/rung-static-numerals-spec`: `4d2d895e8b` (the specification, 9 files, +475 −298) and `d3782350df` (`revival-numeral-type`'s power with a numeral exponent, 1 file). The worktree was seeded by `seed-worktree.sh` ("seeded from /home/user/fortress-base30 (dd00743d9e) in 3 s", exit 0) and its branch pushed.

## What changed and why

The decisions on record, the static numerals (P-174, P-176), with P-173's conversion, default and fold, P-40's bound for sizes, P-165's `asFloat`, P-37's exception for the prelude, and P-96's revision form, are written into the specification. The field numerals' sentences and boxes, climb batch 29's (`7daf51fe8a`), are replaced; Appendix I's `revival-numerals` is rewritten in place (fork T1), and no box names the field numerals. The Effects state the implementations as rung A leaves them (`CLIMB-BATCH-29b.md:222-256` and forks A1 to A8, `:191-206`), with rows 957's second case and 971 written as open (forks A5, A6); the gather corrects them to what lands.

Passage by passage (lines after the change; "before" at b5b0f82c13):

1. **The numeral types** (`literals.tex:98-122`; before `:98-116`). Before: "Every numeral has the type \TYP{Numeral} ... through one of the two types that \TYP{Numeral} comprises ... \Library\ declare these numbers as the getters \VAR{digits}, \VAR{fractionDigits}, \VAR{radix} and \VAR{digitValue} ... They are fields of the numeral's value, not static parameters of its type: the three numeral types have no static parameters." After: "Every numeral has a \emph{numeral type} of its own, which exists only when the program is compiled: no value of a numeral type exists when the program runs. The static arguments of a numeral type are the numeral's \emph{four numbers}: ... Each of the four is a natural number, of any size. A numeral containing only digits has the type `NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\]`, and a numeral containing a radix point has the type `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,r,v\]`. So `3.125` has the type `RadixPointNumeral[\4,3,10,3125\]`, `007` the type `NaturalNumeral[\3,10,7\]`, and `3000000000` the type `NaturalNumeral[\10,10,3000000000\]`." The hierarchy: `Numeral` extends `Number` with no static parameters; `NaturalNumeral` below `AnyNaturalNumeral`, `RadixPointNumeral` below `AnyRadixPointNumeral`, which exclude each other; none declares a method. Reason: P-174; PROBE `12. Decisions`, decision 1; fork A4 (`CLIMB-BATCH-29b.md:202`); the team's two notes kept (`literals.tex:123-138`). Box: `revival-numerals` at `:146`.
2. **The radix** (`literals.tex:140-145`; before `:134-138`). Before: "such a numeral has the same type as one without an indicator. So `deadc_16` is a \TYP{NaturalNumeral} whose four numbers are $5$, $0$, $16$ and $912092$." After: "such a numeral has one of the same two numeral types, with its radix as the static argument $r$. So `deadc_16` has the type `NaturalNumeral[\5,16,912092\]`." Reason: P-174, the radix is `r`; PROBE `14. Where the Draft`.
3. **The box on the numeral types** (`literals.tex:146-161`, `revival-numerals`; before `:139-153`). Before: "The revival decided on 8~November 2026 that the four numbers are fields of the numeral's value: the two types with an explicit radix fold into the radix, and \TYP{Literal} into the digit count ... \TYP{Numeral} comprises the two numeral types." After: "The revival decided on 9~November 2026 that a numeral's type is the Working Draft's \TYP{NaturalNumeral} or \TYP{RadixPointNumeral}, at the Working Draft's arities, with the radix as the static argument $r$, and that it exists only when the program is compiled: the two types with an explicit radix are not built, since $r$ gives the radix, nor is \TYP{Literal}, and \TYP{Numeral} has no static parameters. So the team's draft notes above are answered: no value of a numeral type exists when a program runs, and this section gives the hierarchy of the numeral types." Fork T1.
4. **The conversion** (`literals.tex:165-197`; before `:155-175`). The Draft's sentences kept as batch 29 kept them (`:165-180`). Before: "each of the eight number types ... declares a coercion from \TYP{NaturalNumeral}, and ... one from \TYP{RadixPointNumeral}; the conversion is exact ...". After: the same coercions, "each generic over the four numbers, as \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} declares `coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\])`. The parameter of such a coercion has no value: its body computes the type's value from the four numbers, which it reads as values, integers of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} (\secref{natparams}). ... At a numeral, the compiler instantiates the coercion at the numeral's four numbers and evaluates it: a value that the Java Virtual Machine holds as an `int`, a `long`, a `float` or a `double` is a constant of the compiled code, and any other value, as one of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} or \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, is made once for the place where the numeral stands". Reason: P-174, P-176, P-40; the section's bullet; the declarations of the patch (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-30/probes/draft-numerals.patch:1-207`, `:760-858`).
5. **A place that fixes a type** (`literals.tex:199-201`; before `:177-180`). Before: "... as each number type of \library\ does and a type of a program's own may, or is a numeral type itself." After: the last clause removed. Reason: P-174's written-only rule; PROBE `1. Where the snapshot`; the patch refuses a binding at a numeral type (`tests/NumeralTypeNoValueWalk.fss`, `compiler_tests/LiteralTypeUnwritable.fss`). P-173's "is a numeral type" is not written (reserved point).
6. **A type of a program's own** (`literals.tex:229-267`; before `:207-229`). Before: "receives a numeral through its own coercion from the numeral's type, such as `coerce(x: RadixPointNumeral)`, whose body reads the four numbers ... a negative constant reaches it as the prefix operator \EXP{-} ... Inside the body of a coercion, two values of a numeral type are equal, and strictly equivalent, when their values $v/r^m$ are equal". After: the coercion generic over the four numbers, with the Working Draft's interval as a Fortress block (`:235-241`, P-174's example: `coerce[\nat n, nat m, nat r, nat v\](x: RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]) = Interval(roundDown(v, r, m), roundUp(v, r, m))`); no coercion, no chain, a static error; "The coercion receives the four numbers of a numeral as written. A numeral as written under the prefix operator \EXP{-}, as \EXP{-3}, is that operator of the type applied to the coercion's result for the numeral, so a type without that operator refuses it; any other static expression of numerals alone is folded first ... and reaches the type only through the type's coercion from the folded constant's default type, as \EXP{1/2} through a coercion from \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}"; a `where` clause that compares the four numbers, a static error, as `300` at a byte type with `where {v < 256}`; once per place "with the type's prefix \EXP{-} where the numeral is negated"; written only as a parameter type, "nor as a type that a trait or an object extends". The sentence on two numeral values inside a coercion's body is removed. Reason: P-174 (sign, chain, written-only), P-176, fork A4, fork T3, SNAP `3. The design` point 8 (the byte type) and `11. Consequences`.
7. **The box after it** (`literals.tex:268-285`, `revival-numerals`; before `:230-245`). Before: "The revival decided on 8~November 2026 that ... a type of a program's own receives a numeral only through its coercion from the numeral's type, once for each place; and that the numeral types are written only as parameter types." After: 8 November for the conversion where it stands, the written-only rule and the minus; "It decided on 9~November 2026 that every number type, of \library\ and of a program, receives a numeral through a coercion generic over the four numbers, which the compiler instantiates at the numeral and folds, and that a numeral at a place denotes one value, made once, the same on both implementations. The interpreter, which has no static types, applies the coercion at the place's first evaluation and refuses a numeral only there"; `IntLiteral` "the name that the compiled path's own library gave it".
8. **The box on static rational expressions** (`literals.tex:313-320`; before `:268-273`). Gains: "since at a number type of \library\ it is converted from its exact value; a type of a program's own receives it through its coercion from the constant's default type." Fork T3.
9. **The types chapter** (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:576-588`; before `:576-583`). Before: "\TYP{Numeral}, whose values carry a numeral's four numbers ... as fields", box "the revival decided on 8~November 2026 that they are fields of the numeral's value". After: "the numeral types below \TYP{Numeral}, `NaturalNumeral[\n,r,v\]` and `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,r,v\]`, which exist only when a program is compiled, for appropriate values of \VAR{b}, \VAR{n}, \VAR{m}, \VAR{r}, and \VAR{v}"; box: 9 November, the static arguments, no value when a program runs.

Before: "Each type that coerces from a numeral type declares \EXP{=} with it, ... so that \EXP{u = 0} is \VAR{true} for a zero \VAR{u} of any of the eight types"; "The two numeral types declare \VAR{asFloat} too". After: "A numeral has a numeral type of its own, whose static arguments are the numeral's four numbers, and from which \library\ define coercions to the number types, generic over those numbers"; the box gains the 9 November sentence. The box at `:188` stands (it names no numeral type's form).

## Revival change

**The change.**
- The team's source: the Working Draft gives a numeral six types, `NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\]` (and `Literal[\v\]` without leading zeros), `NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[\n,r,v\]`, `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,10,v\]`, `RadixPointNumeralWithExplicitRadix[\n,m,r,v\]` and `Numeral[\n,m,r,v\]` above all (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-129`), says that "Numerals are not directly converted to any of the number types" (`:132-141`) and that libraries define coercions from numerals (`:146-148`), and says nothing of a numeral's value when a program runs or of when a coercion is applied. The team's compiled library types numerals by run-time values, `trait IntLiteral` and `trait FloatLiteral` with getters such as `asZZ32` and `asRR64` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:390`, `:479`, at b5b0f82c13), whose coercions run on that value.
- What the text now says: a numeral's type exists only at compile time, `NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]` or `RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]`, at the Draft's arities with the radix as `r`, below a `Numeral` without static parameters; the explicit-radix types and `Literal` are not built; no value of a numeral type exists when a program runs, so a numeral type has no method, no `asFloat` and no `=` with a number type; every number type, the library's and a program's, takes a numeral through `coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\])` or its radix-point form, whose body reads the four numbers as `ZZ` values; the compiler folds it to a constant, or makes the value once per place; `-3` at a program's type is the type's own `-` on the coercion's result for `3`; a `where` clause over the four numbers refuses a numeral statically (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:98-285`; `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5010-5486`). The tests that show the tree doing so land with the code: `ProjectFortress/tests/NumeralStaticDesignWalk.fss`, `ProjectFortress/tests/NumeralOwnTypeWalk.fss`, `ProjectFortress/tests/NumeralTypeNoValueWalk.fss`, `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NumeralStaticDesignCompiled.fss` and `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXNumeralWhereRefusedCompiled.test`.
- The reason, as evidence: the Draft's own ground, "This approach allows library designers to decide how numerals should interact with other types of objects by defining coercion operations" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:142-145`), which a coercion that sees only a value cannot carry out: a 16-bit float type's coercion from the four numbers rounds `1.00390625000000000001` once, to `0x3F81`, where a coercion from an `RR64` gives `0x3F80` (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NumeralStaticDesignCompiled.fss`, "BF16(1.00390625000000000001) rounds once, to 0x3F81"); a JVM class file holds no object constant, so a value at a place is a constant or a field filled once when the class loads; the team's own word on the run-time value, "IntLiterals should always be transient objects with minimal lifetime" (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FIntLiteral.java:21-23` at b5b0f82c13).
